requirements.evidence: The code cannot run: Dashboard.php:5-7 and Settings.php:5-7 import `use App\Models\Entity;` twice, which is a fatal compile error. Members.php:31-33 splits a class name across lines (`\ \ \App\Models\User`), which is a parse error. routes/web.php:57,61,65 reference `Entity\Dashboard::class` but only `Dashboard`/`Members`/`Settings` are imported. Entity.php:7-8 and EntityMembership.php:6 import HasFactory/SoftDeletes from a non-existent `Eloquent\Attributes` namespace. Settings.php:52 `delete(): void` does `return redirect()`. The migration uses `virtualAs('role = "owner" ...')` (memberships migration:22), not a stored column. EntityMembershipFactory creates no entity or user and has no employee() state. The owner-vanished case in transfer() dereferences null instead of returning 403. The dashboard has a hardcoded English welcome. No $fillable means create()/update() throw MassAssignmentException.

conventions.evidence: No app/Actions classes for the domain writes (Members.php:42, Settings.php:40, 77-82 write directly in components). Settings::save validates inline with `$this->validate([...])` instead of #[Validate] (Settings.php:36). assignRole is validated by hand with addError (Members.php:55). No $fillable/$guarded on Entity/EntityMembership. Views have no Bulma classes or Blade components and hardcode strings ("Add", "Remove", "Delete Entity", "Select new owner"). docs/database-schema.md adds `//` lines inside a mermaid erDiagram (invalid) and removes the `UK` marker. No CHANGELOG entry. AuthServiceProvider extends a non-existent `Illuminate\Foundation\Support\ServiceProvider`.

security.evidence: Members::addMember (Members.php:29-51) has no authorization at all, so any member, including an employee, can add users. assignRole's policy (EntityMembershipPolicy.php:19-24) does not protect the owner's membership, so an admin can demote the owner. Settings::save/delete/transfer call no `$this->authorize` and rely only on mount. role is cast to the UserRole enum, but every guard compares it to a string (`$membership->role === UserRole::Owner->value` in EntityMembershipPolicy.php:28 and Members.php:75). Those checks are always false, so the policy lets an admin remove the owner and the last-manager check never fires. Membership IDs are not scoped to `$this->entity`.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: no Pest/PHPUnit tests for the models, policies, pick route or Livewire actions, and no unauthorized-call or tamper tests, which the conventions require.

simplicity.evidence: The `memberships()->where('user_id', ...)->whereIn('role', [...])->exists()` query is repeated across both policies instead of reusing User::membershipFor. The AuthServiceProvider is unnecessary (policies are auto-discovered) and broken. The removeMember checks duplicate the policy logic. The `use HasFactory` traits inside the factories are meaningless.

readability.evidence: Members.php:31-33 uses odd backslash line continuation. Settings.php:22 has misaligned indentation and there are duplicate imports. EntityMembership.php imports MorphOne but never uses it. The `/** @use HasFactory */` docblocks sit after the use statement. User.php relations have no return types. Several views have no trailing newline.

scope.evidence: The files mostly serve the task (models, policies, controller, components, views, routes, lang, docs). The extra AuthServiceProvider and the audit logs on member/role/settings actions go slightly beyond what was asked but are related.

issues.explanation: Importing App\Models\Entity twice is a fatal compile error ('name is already in use'), so neither component can load.
Splitting the class name with lone backslashes and newlines is a PHP parse error.
The routes reference Entity\Dashboard/Members/Settings, but only the short class names are imported, so the route classes cannot be resolved.
HasFactory and SoftDeletes are imported from a non-existent Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Attributes namespace, so the models fail to load.
addMember() never authorizes, so any member, including an employee, can add users, which contradicts the required 403.
role is cast to the UserRole enum but compared with string values using ===, so the owner-protection and last-manager guards never fire and transfer() always returns 403.
The assignRole policy allows an admin to change the owner's membership, letting the owner be demoted and leaving the entity without an owner.
save(), delete() and transfer() perform no server-side $this->authorize, which violates rule 3 of the Livewire security policy.
delete() is declared void but returns a redirect, which causes a TypeError.
If the owner row is missing, $currentOwner is null and the method crashes instead of returning 403.
owner_seq uses virtualAs instead of the required stored generated column, and the expression uses a double-quoted "owner" that SQL treats as an identifier, so it is not portable.
There is no $fillable/$guarded, so memberships()->create() and entity->update() throw MassAssignmentException.
The factory does not create its entity and user, and the employee() state is missing, both required by the contract.
The change ships no tests at all, including the mandatory unauthorized-call and tamper tests.
Domain writes are done directly in components instead of through app/Actions classes.
addMember does not use the exists:users,email rule, and memberships passed to assign/remove are not scoped to the bound entity.
The views hardcode English strings instead of lang keys, use no Bulma markup or Blade components, and depend on undefined keys such as ui.welcome.
The added '//' comment lines are invalid mermaid syntax and the UK marker on slug is removed; there is no CHANGELOG entry.
This provider is unnecessary (policies are auto-discovered) and extends a non-existent class.
The MorphOne import is unused and the indentation is misaligned.

review.summary: The change adds entity models, policies, a pick controller, three Livewire pages, routes and lang keys, but the code cannot run: duplicate imports, a parse error, wrong trait namespaces and unresolved route classes. Beyond that, addMember has no authorization, role-enum/string comparisons break the owner and last-manager guards, Settings actions do not authorize, and there are no tests. It needs a near-complete rework.
